moon_mons_mouton.name: Mons Mouton Plateau (Lunar South Pole, Artemis III candidate region)
moon_mons_mouton.description: Flat-topped massif near the lunar south pole, one of NASA's nine candidate landing regions for Artemis III (Oct 2024). Terrain profile computed from LRO LOLA topography over the summit plateau.

center.note: Centre of the flat summit plateau (≈4.4–5.5 km elevation) as read from LRO LOLA by Analog MX; Mons Mouton summit is listed at 84°36′S 31°00′E.

slope_median_deg.source_note: Median slope computed by Analog MX from NASA LRO LOLA 118 m DEM over a 40×30 km box at ~460 m pixels (same method as Earth cells; pipeline/target_terrain.py).

slope_p90_deg.source_note: 90th-percentile slope computed by Analog MX from NASA LRO LOLA 118 m DEM over a 40×30 km box at ~460 m pixels (same method as Earth cells; pipeline/target_terrain.py).

relief_m.source_note: P95−P5 elevation computed by Analog MX from NASA LRO LOLA 118 m DEM over a 40×30 km box at ~460 m pixels (same method as Earth cells; pipeline/target_terrain.py).

real_values_for_display.label: Artemis III candidate region
real_values_for_display.value: One of nine candidate regions announced by NASA, Oct 2024

real_values_for_display.label: South-polar cold traps (Diviner)
real_values_for_display.value: Average annual temperature ≈37 K at the LCROSS site in Cabeus

earth_cannot_simulate: Hard vacuum — no air for convective cooling, no wind
Radiation environment (no magnetic field or atmosphere)
Low-angle polar sunlight, long shadows and permanently shadowed regions
Lunar regolith: sharp, electrostatically charged dust

mars_gale.name: Gale Crater (Curiosity rover site, gypsum-bearing)
mars_gale.description: 155 km crater where Curiosity has driven since 2012; its layered central mound holds sulfates such as gypsum. Terrain profile computed from MGS MOLA topography around Bradbury Landing.

slope_median_deg.source_note: Median slope computed by Analog MX from NASA MGS MOLA 463 m DEM over a 40×30 km box at ~460 m pixels (same method as Earth cells; pipeline/target_terrain.py).

slope_p90_deg.source_note: 90th-percentile slope computed by Analog MX from NASA MGS MOLA 463 m DEM over a 40×30 km box at ~460 m pixels (same method as Earth cells; pipeline/target_terrain.py).

relief_m.source_note: P95−P5 elevation computed by Analog MX from NASA MGS MOLA 463 m DEM over a 40×30 km box at ~460 m pixels (same method as Earth cells; pipeline/target_terrain.py).

real_values_for_display.label: Gypsum link to Earth
real_values_for_display.value: Gale chosen partly because its central mound is thought to hold gypsum; Cuatro Ciénegas is a gypsum-rich analog

real_values_for_display.label: Air temperature at Gale (REMS)
real_values_for_display.value: Daily highs ≈0 °C, lows ≈−70 °C (first months of the mission)
